title: MCP Apps on the Stateless Protocol

questions.question: Where should a modern MCP App bind its UI resource to a tool?
options: Only in the final text result
In a standalone HTTP GET stream
In the tool definition returned by tools/list
questions.explanation: Nested _meta.ui.resourceUri on the tool definition lets the host preload and review the UI before invocation.

questions.question: How does a 2026-07-28 client advertise MCP Apps support?
questions.explanation: Extensions are opt-in through the per-request client capabilities map.

questions.question: What does ui/initialize initialize?
options: The Apps postMessage bridge between an iframe and host
questions.explanation: ui/initialize belongs to the Apps bridge dialect and is separate from the removed MCP core handshake.

questions.question: Which resource response is safest for a user-independent bundled App?
options: No resultType and no cache policy
resultType complete, a bounded ttlMs, public cacheScope, and deny-first CSP
A session token embedded in the HTML
An unlimited ttlMs and wildcard CSP domains
questions.explanation: A complete result, explicit cache hints, and a narrow CSP make the wire and browser policies inspectable.

questions.question: A host receives a resources/read body for one URI but a different Mcp-Name header. What should happen?
questions.explanation: Routing headers and the body must match before version support or feature policy is evaluated; the transport returns HTTP 400 with JSON-RPC error -32020.

questions.question: What is the correct fallback for a host without MCP Apps support?
options: Return HTML as trusted host chrome
Keep the tool usable with ordinary text or structured output and omit the UI binding
Create a hidden session and retry
questions.explanation: An optional extension must not make the underlying tool unusable for clients that do not negotiate it.
